name: Car
title: Car mechanics (1.8 L four-cylinder, 5-speed manual)
intro: This is a front-wheel-drive manual car. Explode it (🧩) to lift the body and see the engine, gearbox, differential and chassis. Ask me "How do the pistons turn the wheels?"
suggest: How do the pistons turn the wheels?
Why does the camshaft turn slower than the crankshaft?
What does the differential do in a turn?
looksLike: car, sedan, saloon, SUV, car engine, tyre, brake disc, steering wheel, gearbox

ride.hint: You're in the driver's seat (the body is off, like a convertible). Drag to look around; open the throttle and change gear to see how engine rpm and speed change; tap X-ray to see the engine and gearbox in front of you.

block.name: Engine block
block.info: Four-cylinder engine block. Pistons move up and down inside while coolant flows through passages in the block walls.

head.name: Cylinder head
head.info: Mounted atop the block, housing the combustion chambers, intake and exhaust valves, and spark plugs.

valve_cover.name: Valve cover
valve_cover.info: Top cover sealing the camshafts and valve train to keep oil inside.

oil_pan.name: Oil pan
oil_pan.info: Bottom oil reservoir from which the oil pump draws lubricant for the crankshaft, rods and pistons.

crankshaft.name: Crankshaft
crankshaft.info: Main engine shaft. Offset crank pins take the push from four connecting rods to turn reciprocating motion into rotation.

crank_pulley.name: Crank pulley
crank_pulley.info: Front pulley on the crankshaft driving the timing belt, alternator and A/C compressor.

flywheel.name: Flywheel
flywheel.info: Heavy disc on the crankshaft that stores rotational inertia to smooth out power pulses and mates with the clutch.

piston_1.name: Piston 1
piston_1.info: Cylinder 1 piston, pushed down by expanding combustion gas to turn the crankshaft via its connecting rod.

piston_2.name: Piston 2
piston_2.info: Cylinder 2 piston, pushed down by expanding gas to turn the crankshaft via its connecting rod.

piston_3.name: Piston 3
piston_3.info: Cylinder 3 piston, pushed down by expanding gas to drive the crankshaft.

piston_4.name: Piston 4
piston_4.info: Cylinder 4 piston, pushed down by expanding gas to drive the crankshaft.

conrod_1.name: Connecting rod 1
conrod_1.info: Links piston 1 to the crankshaft; its top moves vertically while its bottom orbits the crank pin.

conrod_2.name: Connecting rod 2
conrod_2.info: Links piston 2 to the crankshaft, converting vertical motion into rotation.

conrod_3.name: Connecting rod 3
conrod_3.info: Links piston 3 to the crankshaft, converting vertical motion into rotation.

conrod_4.name: Connecting rod 4
conrod_4.info: Links piston 4 to the crankshaft, converting vertical motion into rotation.

camshaft_intake.name: Intake camshaft
camshaft_intake.info: Opens the intake valves in sequence. Spins at half the crankshaft speed because intake happens once every two crank turns.

camshaft_exhaust.name: Exhaust camshaft
camshaft_exhaust.info: Opens the exhaust valves in order at half the crankshaft speed.

timing_belt.name: Timing belt
timing_belt.info: Toothed belt keeping the crankshaft and camshafts at an exact 2:1 ratio so valves open on time.

intake_manifold.name: Intake manifold
intake_manifold.info: Branching pipes that distribute air evenly to all four cylinders.

exhaust_manifold.name: Exhaust manifold
exhaust_manifold.info: Collects exhaust gas from all four cylinders into a single pipe.

exhaust.name: Exhaust
exhaust.info: Routes exhaust through the catalytic converter and muffler before exiting at the rear.

radiator.name: Radiator
radiator.info: Front radiator where oncoming airflow cools hot engine coolant before it circulates back.

battery.name: Battery
battery.info: 12-volt battery that powers the starter motor and runs electronics when the engine is off.

gearbox.name: Gearbox
gearbox.info: The case around the gears. With a transverse engine, the gearbox and differential are built as one unit.

input_shaft.name: Input shaft
input_shaft.info: Spins with the engine when the clutch is engaged, driving the gears on the output shaft.

output_shaft.name: Output shaft
output_shaft.info: Driven by the selected gear pair to send power into the differential.

gear_1.name: 1st gear
gear_1.info: 1st gear on the output shaft: the biggest, providing maximum torque and lowest speed for starting off.

gear_2.name: 2nd gear
gear_2.info: 2nd gear on the output shaft: slightly smaller than 1st.

gear_3.name: 3rd gear
gear_3.info: 3rd gear on the output shaft: the gear engaged right now (drawn in brass).

gear_4.name: 4th gear
gear_4.info: 4th gear on the output shaft: gear ratio close to one to one for steady cruising.

gear_5.name: 5th gear
gear_5.info: Smallest output gear, keeping engine rpm low for fuel-efficient highway cruising.

differential.name: Differential
differential.info: Its 59-tooth ring gear gives final speed reduction, while inner spider gears let the outer wheel spin faster than the inner wheel in turns.

driveshaft_l.name: Left driveshaft
driveshaft_l.info: Sends power from the differential to the left front wheel via constant-velocity (CV) joints that flex as the wheel steers and bounces.

driveshaft_r.name: Right driveshaft
driveshaft_r.info: Sends power from the differential to the right front wheel through CV joints.

knuckle_fl.name: Left steering knuckle
knuckle_fl.info: Holds the left front wheel and brake, pivoting around the kingpin axis when pushed by the tie rod.

knuckle_fr.name: Right steering knuckle
knuckle_fr.info: Holds the right front wheel and brake, pivoting to steer the wheel.

wheel_fl.name: Left front wheel
wheel_fl.info: Left front wheel; on a front-wheel-drive car it both drives and steers.

disc_fl.name: Left front brake disc
disc_fl.info: Ventilated iron disc spinning with the left front wheel, clamped by the caliper to brake.

caliper_fl.name: Left front brake caliper
caliper_fl.info: Hydraulic pressure pushes its piston to clamp brake pads onto the left front disc.

wheel_fr.name: Right front wheel
wheel_fr.info: Right front wheel, handling both propulsion and steering.

disc_fr.name: Right front brake disc
disc_fr.info: Ventilated iron disc spinning with the right front wheel, squeezed by the caliper when braking.

caliper_fr.name: Right front brake caliper
caliper_fr.info: Hydraulic pressure pushes its piston to clamp brake pads onto the right front disc.

wheel_rl.name: Left rear wheel
wheel_rl.info: Non-driven rear wheel that rolls along with the car.

disc_rl.name: Left rear brake disc
disc_rl.info: Brake disc spinning with the left rear wheel.

caliper_rl.name: Left rear brake caliper
caliper_rl.info: Hydraulically clamps the left rear disc to help slow the car.

wheel_rr.name: Right rear wheel
wheel_rr.info: Non-driven rear wheel that rolls along with the car.

disc_rr.name: Right rear brake disc
disc_rr.info: Brake disc spinning with the right rear wheel.

caliper_rr.name: Right rear brake caliper
caliper_rr.info: Hydraulically clamps the right rear disc to help slow the car.

strut_fl.name: Left front strut
strut_fl.info: MacPherson strut combining coil spring and shock absorber to support weight and damp bumps.

control_arm_fl.name: Left front lower control arm
control_arm_fl.info: Links the subframe to the bottom of the knuckle, allowing vertical wheel travel while holding fore-aft position.

strut_fr.name: Right front strut
strut_fr.info: Right MacPherson strut combining spring and damper to support and smooth the ride.

control_arm_fr.name: Right front lower control arm
control_arm_fr.info: Links the subframe to the right knuckle to locate the wheel.

subframe.name: Subframe
subframe.info: Front steel cradle that supports the engine, gearbox and front suspension.

rear_axle.name: Rear axle
rear_axle.info: Torsion-beam rear axle linking both rear wheels with a twistable beam.

spring_rl.name: Left rear spring
spring_rl.info: Supports rear weight and compresses to absorb road bumps.

shock_rl.name: Left rear shock absorber
shock_rl.info: Damper that forces oil through tiny orifices, turning spring bounce into heat so the car settles quickly.

spring_rr.name: Right rear spring
spring_rr.info: Supports rear weight and compresses to absorb road bumps.

shock_rr.name: Right rear shock absorber
shock_rr.info: Hydraulic damper that stops the rear spring from bouncing repeatedly.

steering_wheel.name: Steering wheel
steering_wheel.info: Turning the wheel rotates the steering column and rack to steer the front wheels.

steering_column.name: Steering column
steering_column.info: Shaft linking the steering wheel to the rack; includes universal joints and collapses in a crash.

steering_rack.name: Steering rack
steering_rack.info: Rack-and-pinion mechanism that converts steering rotation into side-to-side motion to push the wheel knuckles.

fuel_tank.name: Fuel tank
fuel_tank.info: Mounted safely under the rear seat; an electric pump inside feeds fuel to the engine injectors.

body.name: Body
body.info: Unibody steel shell: front and rear crumple zones absorb crash energy while the rigid cabin protects passengers. Explode (🧩) to lift it.

hood.name: Bonnet
hood.info: Covers the engine bay, hinged near the windscreen so the front lifts open for servicing.

door_fl.name: Left front door (driver)
door_fl.info: Front-hinged so wind pressure pushes it shut at speed; houses an internal side-impact crash beam.

door_fr.name: Right front door
door_fr.info: Front-hinged passenger door with an internal side-impact beam.

door_rl.name: Left rear door
door_rl.info: Left rear passenger door with an internal side-impact beam.

door_rr.name: Right rear door
door_rr.info: Right rear passenger door with an internal side-impact beam.

trunk.name: Boot lid
trunk.info: Rear boot lid hinged below the back window.

seat_fl.name: Driver's seat
seat_fl.info: Left-hand-drive driver's seat facing the steering wheel and pedals.

seat_rear.name: Back seat
seat_rear.info: Rear passenger bench located just ahead of the rear axle.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.info: Displays speed and engine rpm, with climate and audio controls in the centre and wiring hidden behind.

floor_pan.name: Floor pan and firewall
floor_pan.info: Cabin floor pan. The front slope is the firewall isolating the hot engine bay; the centre tunnel clears the exhaust pipe.

pedals.name: Pedals (clutch, brake, accelerator)
pedals.info: Manual pedals from left to right: clutch, brake, accelerator. Pressing the brake pushes a rod through the firewall to the booster.

brake_booster.name: Brake booster and master cylinder
brake_booster.info: The vacuum booster multiplies your foot force using engine vacuum; the master cylinder converts that push into hydraulic pressure for all four calipers.

drives.engine: Engine idling (crankshaft, pistons, camshafts; in neutral)
drives.power: Driving in 3rd (engine → gearbox → differential → front wheels)
drives.steer: Steering left and right (the front wheels follow)
drives.open: Opening the doors, bonnet and boot

steps.say: The fuel-air mixture ignites and expands rapidly inside the cylinder, pushing the piston down.

quiz.q: When the fuel-air mixture ignites in the cylinder, the piston is…
options: pushed down by expanding gas
Expanding gas drives the piston down—the only stroke of the four that produces power.
sucked up
Combustion expands gas downward; the crankshaft's momentum pushes the piston back up.

steps.say: The connecting rod's top moves up and down while its bottom orbits the offset crank pin, turning linear push into rotation.

quiz.q: When pistons 1 and 4 are at the top, where are pistons 2 and 3?
options: At the bottom
The crank pins are paired 180° apart so 1 & 4 balance 2 & 3, reducing engine vibration.
Also at the top
All four moving together would shake severely, so they are paired 180° apart.
Halfway down
An inline four's crank pins point only two ways: up or down.

steps.say: Via the timing belt, the crankshaft drives both camshafts at half speed to open intake and exhaust valves on time.

quiz.q: When the crankshaft turns twice, how many times does the camshaft turn?
options: Once
Four strokes take two crank turns, and each valve opens only once per cycle.
Twice
Turning twice would open the valves during compression and power strokes, ruining the cycle.
Four times
The camshaft runs at half the crankshaft's speed, not faster.

steps.say: Firing in 1-3-4-2 order, one cylinder produces power every half turn of the crank, while the flywheel smooths the rotation.

power.title: How the engine's force reaches the wheels

steps.say: With the clutch engaged, rotation from the crankshaft and flywheel passes to the gearbox input shaft.
The input shaft drives the engaged 3rd gear on the output shaft, reducing speed and multiplying torque.

quiz.q: When a small gear drives a large gear, the large gear turns…
options: slower, with more torque
Like a longer lever, a larger driven gear trades speed for greater rotational force.
faster, with more torque
Gears trade speed against torque; you cannot increase both at once.
at the same speed
Because the large gear has more teeth, it takes multiple turns of the small gear to turn it once.

steps.say: The output shaft drives the differential for a final speed reduction, sending power through left and right driveshafts to the front wheels.

quiz.q: Which two wheels propel this car?
options: The two front wheels
The engine, gearbox and differential sit in the front and drive the front wheels directly.
The two rear wheels
There are no driveshafts going to the rear axle; the back wheels just roll along.
All four wheels
Four-wheel drive requires a centre propshaft and rear differential, which this car doesn't have.

steps.say: In a corner the outer wheel travels a longer arc; small gears inside the differential let it spin faster than the inner wheel.

quiz.q: When a car corners, which wheel spins faster: the outer or the inner?
options: The outer wheel
The outer wheel follows a wider arc and must cover more ground in the same time.
The inner wheel
The inner wheel takes a tighter, shorter path and turns slower.
Both spin at the same speed
If locked at the same speed, tyres would scrub and skid in corners—that's why cars need a differential.

steer.title: How the steering wheel turns the front wheels

steps.say: Turning the steering wheel rotates the steering column underneath.
A pinion at the bottom of the column moves the toothed rack left and right, pushing the steering knuckles.
The knuckles pivot the front wheels. With a 15:1 steering ratio, turning the wheel 15° steers the road wheels about 1°.

quiz.q: If you turn the steering wheel 180° (half a turn), about how many degrees do the front wheels turn?
options: About 12°
At a 15:1 ratio, 180 ÷ 15 = 12°. This reduction multiplies your force and keeps steering precise.
A 1:1 ratio would make steering impossibly heavy and dangerously twitchy.
Car front wheels only pivot a maximum of 30-some degrees.

brake.title: From brake pedal to a stop

steps.say: Pressing the brake pedal sends hydraulic fluid pressure from the master cylinder to all four brake calipers.
Pistons inside the calipers push brake pads to clamp the spinning brake discs.

quiz.q: What part do the brake calipers clamp onto?
options: The brake discs bolted to the wheels
Each iron disc spins with its wheel, so clamping the disc slows the wheel down.
The rubber tyres
Clamping the rubber tyre would shred it; the iron disc takes the friction instead.
The front driveshafts
There are no rear driveshafts, yet all four wheels need their own disc brakes.

steps.say: Friction converts kinetic energy into hundreds of degrees of heat, so the discs are made of ventilated cast iron to cool down.

belt_snap.title: Broken timing belt
belt_snap.short: The crankshaft turns, but the engine won't start
belt_snap.symptom: You turn the key: the crankshaft and pistons move, yet the engine won't fire up. What's broken?
belt_snap.hint: The camshafts up top must spin to open the valves. Look at the front of the engine: what links the crankshaft pulley to the camshafts?
belt_snap.observe: Watch the spinning crankshaft, then look up at the cylinder head: are the two camshafts turning with it?
whys: A flat battery couldn't crank the engine at all, yet you can see the crankshaft and pistons moving smoothly.
Look inside the block—all four pistons are moving up and down fine. Check what's sitting still at the top of the engine.
belt_snap.cause: The timing belt snapped, so the crankshaft can't drive the camshafts up top and the valves never open.
belt_snap.why: Why won't the engine start when the timing belt breaks, even though the crankshaft is turning?
belt_snap.answer: The timing belt makes the camshafts follow the crankshaft (two crank turns, one cam turn). When it breaks, the valves stay shut, so the cylinders cannot take in fuel-air or exhaust gas.
reasons: The timing belt drives the front wheels directly, so the car can't move without it.
The timing belt carries electricity to the spark plugs, so breaking it stops the spark.
